title: Koszul tensor and tail comparisons preserve Roos projection adjoints
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $t$ a global section such that multiplication by $t$ on $R$ is injective. Put $B_m=R/t^mR$ and $K_m=[R\xrightarrow{t^m}R]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$, augmented to $B_m$, for $m\geq1$. Let $X_\bullet$ be a strict inverse sequence of unbounded $R$-complexes and let $H=R\!\lim_nX_n$ with its projections $p_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Use total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and K-flat derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Countable products of $R$-modules are exact and derived products are represented termwise; write $\mathsf R(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod X_n\to\prod X_n)[-1]$ for the Roos model [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For every $h\geq1$, deleting the levels $n<h$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $\mathsf R(X)\to\mathsf R(X|_{n\geq h})$ compatible with the remaining projections. The canonical tensor/product and cone identifications give a natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Res}_{R\to B_m}(H\otimes_R^LB_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\!\lim_{n\geq h}(X_n\otimes_RK_m)$$
in $D(R)$, where $K_m$ computes the restricted derived tensor. Under it, the projection to $X_n\otimes_RK_m$ is the derived tensor of $p_n$, with the canonical two-term comparison.

More precisely, fix $h=m$, a complex $N$ of $B_m$-modules and a strict compatible family of $B_m$-linear chain maps $f_n:X_n\otimes_RB_m\to N$ for $n\geq m$. Compose the last isomorphism with the derived limit of the augmentations $X_n\otimes_RK_m\to X_n\otimes_RB_m$, then with $R\!\lim f_n$ and the diagonal identification $R\!\lim\operatorname{const}(N)\cong N$. The resulting morphism is the restriction of the adjoint, under the derived tensor--restriction adjunction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], of $H\xrightarrow{p_m}X_m\to\operatorname{Res}N$, the second map being $x\mapsto f_m(x\otimes1)$. Restriction to $D(R)$ detects isomorphisms in $D(B_m)$. These identifications commute with the coefficient quotient transitions: for $k\leq m$ the Koszul transition $K_m\to K_k$ is $(t^{m-k},1)$ in degrees $(-1,0)$. Finally, if all $X_n$ have cohomology in one interval $[a,b]$, then $H$ has cohomology in $[a,b+1]$, without a quasi-compactness hypothesis on $T$.
